summary: The board is built as a set of chips wired together: SH7604, a PS6406B/PS6807 video chip, YMF278B and a 93C56 EEPROM. Each video chip module has chip-style pins (sprite SRAM bus, a 6-way gfx ROM chip-select, WAIT_N, IRQ_N, dot clock). Rendering is a scan-time pipeline driven by HCNT/VCNT: per-line BG register/tile fetch slots, per-line sprite evaluation into double line buffers, and a per-pixel priority sort followed by a 4-step alpha blend chain. MAME instead redraws the whole frame once per priority level (sprites, then BGs, then post-blend) with a z-buffer. What the core shares with MAME is mostly register and bit-field semantics a correct core needs anyway, plus a few alpha conventions.

findings.signal: module per custom chip with chip pins
findings.note: The top level instantiates SH7604, PS6406B, PS6807, YMF278B and E93C56A as separate chips and connects them through CS/RD/WE/WAIT/IRQ wires, with the IRQ going into the SH-2 IRL pins. Nothing is organized around MAME's drawing functions.

findings.signal: external SRAM/ROM bus and wait states
findings.note: The CPU's sprite-RAM and gfx-ROM accesses are held with WAIT_N until a cycle the renderer is not using. The chip drives SRAM_A/OE/WE/CE and decodes ROM_CE_N[5:0] from the ROM address. MAME maps these regions as plain RAM/bank with no contention.

Per-line pre/post colour, scroll, attribute and tile-word reads are placed in fixed (HCNT, DOTCLK_DIV) slots in hblank, interleaved across layers 0/2/1/3, and gfx ROM reads come every 4th dot during active display. MAME instead loops each scanline over a pre-rendered tilemap pixmap.

findings.signal: per-line sprite eval + double line buffer
findings.note: Each line, sprites are evaluated against the line using a stored per-sprite Y phase accumulator, up to 256 hits go into a param RAM, and they are fetched and drawn into alternating line buffers. MAME assembles each zoomed sprite in a temp bitmap and blits it per frame with a z-buffer.

findings.signal: per-pixel priority sort and blend chain
findings.note: For each dot, an insertion sort ranks sprite, BG0-3 and post layers by priority into FST..FTH. The four palette lookups and blends then run in sequence on the four DOTCLK_DIV sub-phases, starting from the pre-line colour. MAME gets the same result by making 8 whole-frame passes, one per priority level.

Writing IACK bit 0 starts a sprite-list load, which clears the bit when done; a vblank-start fallback load also exists. MAME only clears the IRQ in irqctrl_w and latches the sprite list once at screen_vblank.

findings.signal: BG zoom differs from MAME's table
findings.note: The BG X step is a fixed-point increment {1,ZOOM} added once per dot. It does not use MAME's precomputed reciprocal zoom table, so the core's zoom does not come from MAME's maths.
The vidreg, BG attr and sprite word bit-fields (end-of-list bit 14, list in bank 7, BG bank >= 0x0A filter) match MAME's decode. A correct core has to share these.

The core's alpha uses the same 6-to-8-bit replication as MAME's pal6bit, MAME's per-pen alpha for pens 0xC0-0xFF (PIX[7:6]==11), and MAME's post-blend (color&0x7f)<<1 rule. Tie-break order at equal priority (sprites < BG0..3 < post) also follows MAME's draw order. These may be correct behaviour, but they line up with MAME's conventions.

PS4 also follows MAME's register meaning: the list starts at +4 words, bit 15 skips an entry, and bit 13 selects the screen. It is built as a scan-time line buffer per screen, and brightness masks to 0x7F rather than using MAME's clamp/float maths.
